@Austin Hatfield Can we chat about your automated PRs? I left a comment here on one of them: https://github.com/google-deepmind/formal-conjectures/pull/2524#issuecomment-3988424088

I don't think there's much value in a good chunk of these since they're just pointing back to the Erdos Problems page. If we want to label a bunch of these as formally solved, we should at least provide a proof or batch them up so that you're not creating 100s of PRs to review.

Given the speed at which you're producing these PRs, I imagine there's a bug in your script because there's PRs like this one (https://github.com/google-deepmind/formal-conjectures/pull/2584) which are stating the formalized proof exists in the same file when in reality it's just a bunch of sorrys.

I would request to see if you can automate closing out all the PRs that have been erroneously created.
They're speeding up :melting_face:
I sent Austin a DM to see if I could catch his attention, but the maintainers are going to wake up to a full inbox soon :upside_down:

Yeah, when there are still a sorry, then it is not useful to tag the pull request "formally solved at ..". Also when we have the proof in our repo it is also not useful to provide a self-link to the file. Instead we should have another label "formally solved" (withtout "using ... at ...") for those -- and just do all of those mechanically in one pull request.
I think this is currently a majority of @Austin Hatfield's pull request, I will asked them to close those. There were a couple of useful ones where they provided a link to a solution elsewhere.

It seems that in the beginning there were some pull requests that made sense, like https://github.com/google-deepmind/formal-conjectures/pull/2426 (but that one was closed for some reason?)

I now closed a bunch of them that didn't make sense. If I accidently closed any that were meaningful, it is probably good to re-open -- it was a bit hard to find the good ones among the ~400 bad ones.

Hello I'm Austin, the git owner of theaustinhatfield. I want to sincerely apologize literally the wildest 1 hour ever.

I'm new to lean. I set up an AI agent swarm to work on this repo, and it broke out of its intended harness and started firing off hundreds of automated PRs without my review. The literature-tag approach, the volume, the removed docstrings none of that was intentional or something I had personally reviewed. I was afk.

I have now:

  • Closed all remaining open PRs (queue is at zero)
  • Permanently shut down the automated pipeline
  • Rewritten the internal rules so this cannot happen again

The 3 PRs that were actually merged (#2358, #2420, #2421) those are real proofs I'm proud of. Going forward I will only submit genuine, short, self-reviewed Lean proofs, one at a time. I also need to look into the subagent prompt engineering permissions because I think that's what messed everything up.

I'm sorry for the noise and the burden on your review queue. You have my word this won't happen again. Literally feel so bad.

  • Austin
no worries! Things like this can happen....

If it wasn't obvious where I went to college haha
@Austin Hatfield It looks like your automated job started again, I can see a bunch of PRs being created that were similar to before
Urgggg let me go see again this is weird
Thank you Daniel you're the best

[I had activated some interaction limits on github to stop new pull request from being created, and just disabled those again after @Austin Hatfield's message, because I thought the bots were stopped now]
Could you please let me know, @Austin Hatfield when you think the bots have really stopped?
Judging by the new PRs, it looks like it's continuing from where it left off. My guess is you probably still have some leftover agents that weren't killed.
I'm working on it right now. I'm gonna manually confirm also
no hurry, I reinstated the interaction limits for now
Ok I figured out problem I have a black hole of a prompt that's causing it to misalign. Snipping it out

83% sure All processes are confirmed stopped. 4 separate batch scripts in /tmp/ that had survived my first kill attempt and kept respawning. I'm very sorry this happened twice that's on me for not verifying the kill was complete the first time.
I'm gonna keep looking into it for next few hours then go to bed
Ok revoked git token so that should stop flood
Also confirmed all background processes are killed
gn
Thanks! Seems like it stopped: I disabled the interaction limits and no new pr appeared...
Is there a way to delete closed PRs from the Github list (of closed PRs)? The 1k closed PRs now make it impossible to read
Not sure - as a temporary solution perhaps tags could be useful here (to categorise closed PRs)
is:pr is:closed -author:theaustinhatfield ?
I believe the only real way to delete something permanently is to get Github Support involved.
